known_outcome: Holmes rejected this commit: StructuredText::lineMatches returns 0 when preg_match_all fails, and no test can reach that branch, because the test's preg override lives in another namespace.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Part 1: `CleanCode.Strings.MultilineStrings`**

- [ ] AC1. A concatenated valid UTF-8 string with exactly `maximumLines` lines gets no `MultilineStrings.Concatenation` error. Fixtures cover at least three characters whose UTF-8 bytes contain `0x85`: Greek `υ` (`CF 85`), `Ņ` (`C5 85`) and U+2005 (`E2 80 85`). Each fixture has several such characters per line.
- [ ] AC2. The same kind of string with `maximumLines + 1` lines gets exactly one `Concatenation` error. The message states that exact line count. LF, CRLF and a lone CR each count as one line break. The PR states whether a real U+0085, U+2028 or U+2029 counts as a break, and a fixture pins that choice.
- [ ] AC3. A concatenated string that is not valid UTF-8 is still checked, using the byte-mode count the sniff gives today. Two fixtures cover it, with invalid bytes written as escapes such as `"\xCF"`. One is over the limit and is reported, and its message states the byte-mode count. One is at the limit and is not reported. The run raises no PHP warning, notice or exception. A failed match is never taken as a count of zero breaks.
- [ ] AC4. The shared `StructuredText` helper, used by `MultilineStrings` and `RequireHeredocForStructuredText`, never treats a byte inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character as a line break. One fixture per line-break pattern (markdown line, INI section, setting line) puts a character ending in byte `0x85` directly before the shaped text. None of them is classified as structured. The same text with a real newline in that place is still classified as structured. Text that is not valid UTF-8 is classified as it is today, with no PHP warning.
- [ ] AC5. The existing fixtures and expected-error lists for `MultilineStrings` and `RequireHeredocForStructuredText` are not edited, and they all still pass.

**Part 2: `VariableAnalysis.CodeAnalysis.VariableAnalysis.UndefinedVariable` under the CleanCode standard**

- [ ] AC6. A by-reference built-in called with named arguments, followed by a read of the by-reference variable, gives no `UndefinedVariable` error. Fixtures cover at least `preg_match` (`matches:`), `preg_match_all` (`matches:`), `str_replace` (`count:`), `similar_text` (`percent:`) and `parse_str` (`result:`). The by-reference argument appears first, in the middle and last. One fixture mixes positional and named arguments.
- [ ] AC7. A nested arrow function that reads a variable from an enclosing scope gives no `UndefinedVariable` error. Fixtures cover `fn ($a) => array_map(fn ($b) => $a + $b, $items)`, three levels of nested arrow functions, an arrow function inside a closure with `use`, and a nested arrow function inside a method that reads a local variable of the method.
- [ ] AC8. Genuinely undefined variables are still reported. The existing `UndefinedVariable` failing fixture gives the same errors, at the same lines and columns. Each of these is reported:
  - an undefined variable passed by name to a by-value parameter, for example `preg_match(pattern: $p, subject: $undefined)`
  - a read of the by-reference variable before the call that defines it
  - another undefined variable in the same call as a named by-reference argument
  - a nested arrow function that reads a variable no enclosing scope defines

  A call with an unknown named parameter raises no PHP error in phpcs. Turning off or excluding the `UndefinedVariable` code does not meet this criterion.
- [ ] AC9. A consuming repository gets both fixes by updating `mike-bronner/clean-code` alone, with no change to its own `phpcs.xml`. The reported sniff code stays `VariableAnalysis.CodeAnalysis.VariableAnalysis.UndefinedVariable`, so existing excludes and ignore comments keep working. The other `VariableAnalysis` codes behave as before, and the existing `UnusedLocalVariable` tests pass unedited. If the fix needs a newer `sirbrillig/phpcs-variable-analysis`, the lower bound in `composer.json` is the first release that has it.
- [ ] AC10. The PR description records whether upstream `sirbrillig/phpcs-variable-analysis` already fixes, or has an option for, each of the two Part 2 problems. It also says which approach this PR takes.

**Both parts**

- [ ] AC11. Each new fixture case for AC1, AC4, AC6 and AC7 reports an error on the pre-change code and none after the change. Fixtures for AC2, AC3 and AC8 give the same result before and after. The PR names the pre-change commit and quotes the failing test output from that run.
- [ ] AC12. Every statement about what these sniffs report is true of the new behaviour. That covers `README.md`, `resources/boost/skills/clean-code/references/code-style-multiline-strings-heredoc.md`, `resources/boost/skills/clean-code/references/cleancode-undefinedvariable.md`, and any other hit in the repo outside `vendor/` for `MultilineStrings`, `StructuredText` or `UndefinedVariable`.
- [ ] AC13. The full test suite passes, and so does lint under `phpcs.self.xml` and `phpcs.lint.xml`. The changed source has no new `phpcs:ignore` comment. If the fix uses an `mbstring` function, `composer.json` declares `ext-mbstring`.
